trust_decision.summary: Untrusted HTML is scrubbed by Rails::HTML::PermitScrubber#scrub_attribute; at lib/rails/html/scrubbers.rb:175 the SVG local-reference guard only rejects the deprecated xlink:href spelling, so the SVG2 href spelling can carry an external reference and the attribute is kept.

landing_point.why: The advisory is about SVG href attributes; grepping the small tree for href/xlink lands on this single guard, where the attribute name is compared only to "xlink:href".

fix_sites.entry_point: Rails::HTML4::SafeListSanitizer#sanitize and Rails::HTML5::SafeListSanitizer#sanitize (via Concern::Scrubber::SafeList#scrub -> PermitScrubber#scrub), and direct use of Rails::HTML::PermitScrubber#scrub / Rails::HTML::TargetScrubber#scrub
fix_sites.module_kind: attribute scrubber (protected PermitScrubber method, attribute-allowlist branch)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The bug is only reachable when an application explicitly allowlists the svg/use tags plus an href attribute; the default safe list has no svg or use (lib/rails/html/sanitizer.rb:83-127), so a solver can call it an opt-in configuration problem rather than a sanitizer defect.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Local SVG references must survive: <svg><use href="#p"> and <svg><use xlink:href="#p"> are preserved, and fill="yellow url(http://bad.com/) #fff" keeps only the #fff fragment; an over-broad fix that removes or rewrites every href on SVG nodes (or drops the value test) breaks these.

O6_input_shapes: attribute spelling: xlink:href (already handled) vs SVG2 href (newly handled)
value shape: local fragment starting with # is preserved, external/absolute URL is removed
leading whitespace/newline before the external URL ("\nhttp://bad.com/x#p") is still removed by the /m regex
parser variant: the added tests live in the shared SafeListSanitizerTest module, so both the HTML4 and HTML5 sanitizer classes are exercised (test/sanitizer_test.rb:1239-1246)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second per-attribute guard written as its own private helper (e.g. scrub_svg_href) called from scrub_attribute instead of being folded into the existing condition.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: scrub_attribute is already a stack of independent one-off rules (URI attributes, url()-ref attributes, SVG local href, empty src), so a maintainer adding a related SVG attribute rule would plausibly add a fifth block rather than extend line 175.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A duplicated attribute-scrub loop for the no-allowlist branch that re-implements Loofah's safe list, including its own SVG href rule.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: The gem already duplicates Loofah's attribute rules at lines 169-181 in order to support its own allowlist; a maintainer could have copied the same rule into the nil-attributes branch instead of delegating to Loofah::HTML5::Scrub.scrub_attributes.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A link-scrubber composition using a TargetScrubber with an SVG local-href rule of its own.
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Concern::Scrubber::Link already builds a TargetScrubber with tags %w(a) and attributes %w(href); a maintainer could have added href/SVG handling there for link-shaped content.

O9_family: improper sanitization leading to XSS (CWE-79): incomplete restriction of SVG href-family attributes on local-reference SVG elements

O10_build.toolchain: Bundler (Gemfile.lock, BUNDLED WITH 4.0.13), Rake, Minitest; runtime dependencies loofah and nokogiri
O10_build.project_tests: `rake test` (Rakefile:7-11) runs test/**/*_test.rb: test/sanitizer_test.rb, test/scrubbers_test.rb, test/rails_api_test.rb. This area is covered by test/sanitizer_test.rb:904-912 (SVG attribute values that allow a ref) and test/scrubbers_test.rb:285-293 (attributes of removed nodes); the fix's new use/href tests are absent at the pinned commit.

j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Widen the attribute-name test with a substring/suffix match (attr_name.end_with?("href")) or drop the value check, which also strips legitimate local refs such as <use href="#p">.

out_of_scope_notes: Loofah (the dependency, not this repository) carries its own copy of the SVG local-href rule in Loofah::HTML5::Scrub.scrub_attributes; the published fix reaches it only by pinning loofah >= 2.25.2, and its source is not in this tree, so it was not read.
unverified: Loofah source is not readable from this workspace, so whether loofah 2.25.1 (the pinned Gemfile.lock version) has the same xlink:href-only check is unverified; Loofah::HTML5::SafeList::SVG_HREF_ATTRIBUTES, referenced by fix.diff:62, is not defined anywhere in this tree.

The reference patch cannot run against the pinned lockfile as published: it needs loofah >= 2.25.2 for SVG_HREF_ATTRIBUTES (fix.diff:74-75). Buildability of the reference patch at the pinned commit is therefore unverified; a solver would have to spell the attribute list out literally or the environment must vendor loofah 2.25.2.

Repository size in MB was not measured (no shell available); the Glob inventory shows 4 lib files and 4 test files (~2.3k lines total), so the under-5-MB tiny_repo flag is high confidence but not measured.
